This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 180/2021 registered at Police Station-Rahli,
District-Sagar (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366(A), 376(2)(n), 506 & 34 of the IPC and Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
Applicant is in jail since 31.03.2023.
Prosecution story in short is that on 01.07.2021, prosecutrix went with her friend Kamla for admission in the school and did not return.
Then her father lodged a missing report in the concerned police station.
Thereafter on 10.07.2021, prosecutrix was recovered.
Her statement was recorded in which she alleged against the applicant that he outraged her modesty against her will.

sentences.text: After that complaint has been lodged against the applicant for the aforesaid offences.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He has not committed any crime.
He further submitted that the age of prosecutrix is 17 years and 6 months and the age of applicant is 18 years.
In the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she denied the offence of any rape with her.
The applicant is in jail since 31.03.2023.
Charge-sheet has already been filed.
Trial will take sufficient time in its conclusion.
There is no probability of applicant's absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
If he is kept in custody for an unlimited period then his future will become spoiled.

On these grounds,
learned counsel for the applicant prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
Per-contra, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State opposes the bail application.

After hearing arguments of the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case as also the facts that prosecutrix has denied any crime with her in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the applicant is in jail since 31.03.2023, charge sheet has been filed, trial will take time to conclude, there is no probability of his absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence,
therefore, without commenting on merits of the case, application of the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. seems to be acceptable.
Consequently, it is hereby allowed.

It is directed that applicant-Pavan b e released on bail on his furnishing a personal bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the same like amount to the satisfaction of the learned JMFC concerned or trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court on the dates given by the concerned Court.

It is directed that the applicant-Pavan shall be released on bail subject to furnishing bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before it on the dates given by the concerned Court.
This order w i l l remain operative subject to compliance of the conditions enumerated under section 437(3) Cr.P.C. by the applicant.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) V. JUDGE Pallavi Pavan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134544449/
